title: Public speaking has depth
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What do you do when the audience does not take your bait?
Jose said that public speaking is a whole world: we could read ten books on it, and the author does not give it the justice it deserves. He said he wants it to be useful for a plan, not nebulous.
A student said: you have to be ready to back-pedal. If they are not receiving the topic, giving the whole speech on its details goes worse.
Jose said it is like teaching something technical: start broad, then more technical, and know when to back off if the person is not ready.
A student said that some words have deeper meaning, with audience engagement and trust, and using words that resonate with them.
Jose asked why some words change the world and last for centuries, and said the common denominator is the messaging and the impact those messages have, from generation to generation.
He said that in poetry inverting words to create meaning is called inversion, and that once upon a time is an induction that appeals to the imagination.
Jose said that today you may have five seconds of attention, but you can lead people with a powerful deep beginning, the two-minute grab the author describes, into a deeper message.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write how you would back off if they are not ready.
Write your opening that grabs in five seconds.
Write the deeper message it leads to.
Write the words that last in your field.

check.q: What did a student say to be ready to do?
What did Jose say you can do with five seconds of attention?
choices: Lead with a powerful deep beginning

check.q: What did Jose say is the common denominator in lasting works?

recap: Read the room. Grab fast, then go deep.
